The `refresh()` function does not revalidate tagged data. To revalidate tagged data, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead. 417 418 ### Revalidate data 419 420 After performing a mutation, you can revalidate the Next.js cache and show the updated data by calling [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) within the Server Function: 421 422 ```ts filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher 423 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 424 import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache' 425 426 export async function createPost(formData: FormData) { 427 'use server' 428 const session = await auth() 429 if (!session?.user) { 430 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 431 } 432 // Mutate data 433 // ... 434 435 revalidatePath('/posts') 436 } 437 ``` 438 439 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 440 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 441 import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache' 442 443 export async function createPost(formData) { 444 'use server' 445 const session = await auth() 446 if (!session?.user) { 447 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 448 } 449 // Mutate data 450 // ... 451 revalidatePath('/posts') 452 } 453 ``` 454 455 ### Redirect after a mutation 456 457 You may want to redirect the user to a different page after a mutation. You can do this by calling [`redirect`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) within the Server Function. 458 459 ```ts filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher 460 'use server' 461 462 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 463 import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache' 464 import { redirect } from 'next/navigation' 465 466 export async function createPost(formData: FormData) { 467 const session = await auth() 468 if (!session?.user) { 469 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 470 } 471 // Mutate data 472 // ... 473 474 revalidatePath('/posts') 475 redirect('/posts') 476 } 477 ``` 478 479 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 480 'use server' 481 482 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 483 import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache' 484 import { redirect } from 'next/navigation' 485 486 export async function createPost(formData) { 487 const session = await auth() 488 if (!session?.user) { 489 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 490 } 491 // Mutate data 492 // ... 493 494 revalidatePath('/posts') 495 redirect('/posts') 496 } 497 ``` 498 499 Calling `redirect` [throws](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect#behavior) a framework handled control-flow exception. Any code after it won't execute. If you need fresh data, call [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) beforehand. 500 501 ### Cookies 502 503 You can `get`, `set`, and `delete` cookies inside a Server Action using the [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) API. 504 505 When you [set or delete](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies#understanding-cookie-behavior-in-server-functions) a cookie in a Server Action, Next.js re-renders the current page and its layouts on the server so the **UI reflects the new cookie value**. 506 507 > **Good to know**: The server update applies to the current React tree, re-rendering, mounting, or unmounting components, as needed. Client state is preserved for re-rendered components, and effects re-run if their dependencies changed. 508 509 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 510 'use server' 511 512 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 513 514 export async function exampleAction() { 515 const cookieStore = await cookies() 516 517 // Get cookie 518 cookieStore.get('name')?.value 519 520 // Set cookie 521 cookieStore.set('name', 'Delba') 522 523 // Delete cookie 524 cookieStore.delete('name') 525 } 526 ``` 527 528 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 529 'use server' 530 531 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 532 533 export async function exampleAction() { 534 // Get cookie 535 const cookieStore = await cookies() 536 537 // Get cookie 538 cookieStore.get('name')?.value 539 540 // Set cookie 541 cookieStore.set('name', 'Delba') 542 543 // Delete cookie 544 cookieStore.delete('name') 545 } 546 ``` 547 548 ### useEffect 549 550 You can use the React [`useEffect`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffect) hook to invoke a Server Action when the component mounts or a dependency changes. You can do this by calling [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) from `next/cache` in a Server Action: 379 380 ```ts filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher 381 'use server' 382 383 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 384 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 385 386 export async function updatePost(formData: FormData) { 387 const session = await auth() 388 if (!session?.user) { 389 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 390 } 391 // Mutate data 392 // ... 393 394 refresh() 395 } 396 ``` 397 398 ```js filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher 399 'use server' 400 401 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 402 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 403 404 export async function updatePost(formData) { 405 const session = await auth() 406 if (!session?.user) { 407 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 408 } 409 // Mutate data 410 // ... 411 412 refresh() 413 } 414 ``` 415 416 This refreshes the client router, ensuring the UI reflects the latest state. The `refresh()` function does not revalidate tagged data. To revalidate tagged data, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead. 417 418 ### Revalidate data 419 420 After performing a mutation, you can revalidate the Next.js cache and show the updated data by calling [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) within the Server Function: 421 422 ```ts filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher 423 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 424 import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache' 425 426 export async function createPost(formData: FormData) { 427 'use server' 428 const session = await auth() 429 if (!session?.user) { 430 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 431 } 432 // Mutate data 433 // ... 434 435 revalidatePath('/posts') 436 } 437 ``` 438 439 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 440 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 441 import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache' 442 443 export async function createPost(formData) { 444 'use server' 445 const session = await auth() 446 if (!session?.user) { 447 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 448 } 449 // Mutate data 450 // ... 451 revalidatePath('/posts') 452 } 453 ``` 454 455 ### Redirect after a mutation 456 457 You may want to redirect the user to a different page after a mutation. You can do this by calling [`redirect`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) within the Server Function. 458 459 ```ts filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher 460 'use server' 461 462 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 463 import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache' 464 import { redirect } from 'next/navigation' 465 466 export async function createPost(formData: FormData) { 467 const session = await auth() 468 if (!session?.user) { 469 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 470 } 471 // Mutate data 472 // ... 473 474 revalidatePath('/posts') 475 redirect('/posts') 476 } 477 ``` 478 479 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 480 'use server' 481 482 import { auth } from '@/lib/auth' 483 import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache' 484 import { redirect } from 'next/navigation' 485 486 export async function createPost(formData) { 487 const session = await auth() 488 if (!session?.user) { 489 throw new Error('Unauthorized') 490 } 491 // Mutate data 492 // ... 493 494 revalidatePath('/posts') 495 redirect('/posts') 496 } 497 ``` 498 499 Calling `redirect` [throws](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect#behavior) a framework handled control-flow exception. Any code after it won't execute. If you need fresh data, call [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) beforehand. 500 501 ### Cookies 502 503 You can `get`, `set`, and `delete` cookies inside a Server Action using the [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) API. 504 505 When you [set or delete](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies#understanding-cookie-behavior-in-server-functions) a cookie in a Server Action, Next.js re-renders the current page and its layouts on the server so the **UI reflects the new cookie value**. 506 507 > **Good to know**: The server update applies to the current React tree, re-rendering, mounting, or unmounting components, as needed. Client state is preserved for re-rendered components, and effects re-run if their dependencies changed. 508 509 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 510 'use server' 511 512 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 513 514 export async function exampleAction() { 515 const cookieStore = await cookies() 516 517 // Get cookie 518 cookieStore.get('name')?.value 519 520 // Set cookie 521 cookieStore.set('name', 'Delba') 522 523 // Delete cookie 524 cookieStore.delete('name') 525 } 526 ``` 527 528 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 529 'use server' 530 531 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 532 533 export async function exampleAction() { 534 // Get cookie 535 const cookieStore = await cookies() 536 537 // Get cookie 538 cookieStore.get('name')?.value 539 540 // Set cookie 541 cookieStore.set('name', 'Delba') 542 543 // Delete cookie 544 cookieStore.delete('name') 545 } 546 ``` 547 548 ### useEffect 549 550 You can use the React [`useEffect`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffect) hook to invoke a Server Action when the component mounts or a dependency changes. This is useful for mutations that depend on global events or need to be triggered automatically. For example, `onKeyDown` for app shortcuts, an intersection observer hook for infinite scrolling, or when the component mounts to update a view count: 551 552 ```tsx filename="app/view-count.tsx" switcher 553 'use client' 554 555 import { incrementViews } from './actions' 556 import { useState, useEffect, useTransition } from 'react' 557 558 export default function ViewCount({ initialViews }: { initialViews: number }) { 559 const [views, setViews] = useState(initialViews) 560 const [isPending, startTransition] = useTransition() 561 562 useEffect(() => { 563 startTransition(async () => { 564 const updatedViews = await incrementViews() 565 setViews(updatedViews) 566 }) 567 }, []) 568 569 // You can use `isPending` to give users feedback 570 return

Done. I've implemented `ContactForm` in `app/ContactForm.tsx`:

- **Inline server action** — `submitContactMessage` is defined directly inside the component with the `'use server'` directive at the top of the function body. Per the Next.js 16 docs (`mutating-data.md`), this is the supported way to inline a Server Action in a Server Component, and `ContactForm` has no `'use client'` directive so it qualifies.
- **Three fields** — `name`, `email`, and `message`, wired via the form's `action` prop, which automatically passes `FormData` to the action.
- **Validation in the server action** — checks that all three fields are present and throws if any is missing.

It matches the existing convention in `page.tsx` (`formData.get(...) as string`, simulated persistence via `console.log`), and `tsc --noEmit` passes clean.

One note: the inputs also carry the HTML `required` attribute for client-side UX, but the real check lives in the server action as requested — server actions are reachable via direct POST, so server-side validation is what actually guards the data.
